title: UPI merchant discount rate (MDR) on specified P2M payments above INR 2,000
verification_note: Every parameter in this spec is drawn directly from the full text of NPCI's own FAQ (15 Sept 2026), fetched from a mirror hosted by the Department of Financial Services (npci.org.in itself blocks automated fetching, so the DFS mirror of the same PDF was used to read the primary source directly, not secondhand summaries). Each rule below cites its exact question number.

official_source.document: Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Select UPI (P2M) Transactions - Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
official_source.mirror_note: The NPCI-hosted PDF disallows automated fetching (robots.txt); the Department of Financial Services mirror of the identical document was fetched directly and used as the primary source for this spec.

rules.name: Before policy effective date
rules.text: This transaction is dated before the policy's 15 October 2026 effective date, so no MDR was actually charged on it at the time - this framework did not exist yet.

rules.name: Autopay / recurring mandate exemption
rules.text: Automated recurring standing instructions (UPI Mandates / AutoPay) - monthly utility bills, OTT subscriptions, recurring investments/SIPs etc. - carry no prescribed MDR at all, regardless of amount or sector.
rules.source: NPCI FAQ Q22 (verified against primary text)

rules.name: Scope: UPI only
rules.text: MDR applies to specified person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI payments. Cash, card and other methods, and all P2P transfers, are outside this policy.
rules.source: NPCI FAQ Q16 (P2P free), general framework

rules.name: Threshold
rules.text: Only payments ABOVE INR 2,000 can attract MDR. Payments up to and including INR 2,000 remain free - over 95% of UPI P2M volume.

rules.name: Small-merchant (P2PM) exemption
rules.text: Small merchants (P2PM category) receiving up to INR 1 lakh a month through UPI QR payments directly into their own account get zero MDR, regardless of individual transaction size.
rules.assumption: Migration to standard P2M status happens only after inward UPI QR receipts exceed INR 1 lakh for 3 CONSECUTIVE months, and is treated as permanent from that point. Verbatim from Q29: 'Merchants with inward credit of UPI payment more than Rs 1 lakh per month, consecutively for 3 months, are formally transitioned under P2M category.'

rules.name: Sector flat fee
rules.text: Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and utility payments (electricity, water, piped gas) attract a flat INR 5 MDR above INR 2,000 instead of the 0.4% standard rate.
rules.source: NPCI FAQ Q33 (railways/telecom/insurance/fuel, 'among others'), Q39 (insurance), Q40 (fuel), Q41 (utilities)

rules.name: Standard MDR
rules.text: Standard rate is 0.4% on eligible P2M UPI payments above INR 2,000.

rules.name: Standard MDR cap
rules.text: For payments of INR 75,000 and above the standard-rate MDR is capped at INR 300 per transaction - an explicit amount threshold stated by NPCI, not merely a derived breakeven.
rules.source: NPCI FAQ Q3, Q32, Q35 (worked-example table matches exactly: Rs 3,000->Rs 12, Rs 50,000->Rs 200, Rs 75,000+->Rs 300 flat)

rules.name: Unmodelled sector
rules.text: Education-fee payments (school/university/entrance-exam fees) above INR 2,000 get 'flat-fee structures or capped processing rates' per NPCI's own FAQ - but NPCI does not state the exact figure anywhere in the document. Flagged instead of guessed.
rules.source: NPCI FAQ Q42 - the FAQ itself does not give a number here, this is not a gap in our sourcing

rules.name: Consumers do not pay
rules.text: The MDR sits on the merchant side. NPCI states this explicitly and that merchants cannot pass it on to customers. Allocation between merchant and payment providers still depends on the merchant's own contract, so results are reported as estimated exposure.

rules.name: Capital-markets MDR
rules.text: One-time UPI payments to mutual funds (AMCs), SEBI-registered brokers/dealers and investment platforms attract a concessional 0.02% rate instead of the standard 0.4%. A SIP paid via Autopay is exempt under R-00; only a fresh one-time payment (fund purchase, broker wallet top-up, IPO application) falls here.

rules.name: Capital-markets MDR cap
rules.text: The capital-markets rate is capped at INR 300 per transaction, which becomes binding above roughly INR 15 lakh (300 / 0.02%).

rules.name: Credit-linked UPI out of scope
rules.text: UPI payments made via a RuPay credit card linked to UPI, or a pre-sanctioned bank credit line, are governed by separate credit-product rules and are NOT covered by this MDR framework at all - regardless of amount, sector, or anything else in this spec.
